outcomes.text: Talk and write about the three themes using own experiences and those of Bengali-speaking communities.
Discuss relationships with family and friends.
Discuss marriage and partnership.
Discuss social media and its uses.
Discuss mobile technology.
Talk about music.
Talk about cinema and TV.
Talk about food and eating out.
Talk about sport.
Describe customs and festivals in Bengali-speaking countries and communities.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest

outcomes.text: Describe home, town, neighbourhood and region.
Discuss charity and voluntary work.
Discuss healthy and unhealthy living.
Discuss the environment.
Discuss poverty and homelessness.
Talk about travel and tourism.

topics.title: 3.2.1 Listening: understand and respond to spoken language

outcomes.text: Develop listening, speaking, reading and writing skills across the themes.
Understand general and specific content of clear standard spoken Bengali.
Pick out the message, key points, details and opinions, and tell past, present and future apart.
Deduce meaning from longer, more abstract or authentic spoken texts.
Answer questions, extract information, evaluate and conclude from extended spoken text.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Speaking: communicate and interact in speech

outcomes.text: Hold a short conversation, asking and answering questions and exchanging opinions.
Convey information and narrate events coherently.
Speak spontaneously and sustain talk using rephrasing or repair.
Start and develop discussion with extended speech.
Use varied vocabulary and grammar across past, present and future.
Express and justify own views creatively.
Pronounce and intone Bengali so a native speaker understands.

topics.title: 3.2.3 Reading: understand and respond to written language

outcomes.text: Understand general and specific details in familiar written texts.
Identify message, key points, details and opinions in short and longer passages.
Deduce meaning from complex, unfamiliar or authentic texts and short narratives.
Respond to extended texts including adapted literary extracts.
Scan for information, infer and spot implicit meaning.
Translate a short passage from Bengali into English.
Write short texts with simple, accurate sentences.
Write extended text presenting facts, ideas and opinions.
Use varied vocabulary and structures to describe and narrate across time.
Adapt structures, style and register for new purposes.
Make creative, independent use of language to inform or convince.
Translate sentences and short texts from English into Bengali.
Apply Foundation Tier Bengali grammar; receptive structures need recognition only.
Use the noun cases and plural forms of personal nouns.
Use definite and indefinite articles, singular and plural, and the counter word jon.
Use ordinary, demonstrative, interrogative and indefinite adjectives, comparisons and repetition for plurals.
Form adverbs from adjectives and use interrogative adverbs and adverbs of time and place.
Use quantifiers and intensifiers such as khub and onek.
Use demonstrative, personal, interrogative and reflexive pronouns, familiar and polite, in each case.
Use the zero verb, its negative, and achhe for location, possession and states.
Use future, present, past, perfect, habitual and continuous tenses, familiar and polite, with negation.
Use imperatives, the infinitive and verbal noun, and verbs that take an infinitive.
Use participles and common extended and compound verbs.
Use impersonal constructions for liking, need, convenience and illness, and obligation with ought and must.
Use postpositions after genitive and nominative nouns and shomoy for appointments.
Join clauses with conjunctions such as ar, ebong, kintu.
Use idiomatic particles, numbers up to 100 and time telling.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Theme 3: Current and future study and employment

outcomes.text: Talk about own studies.
Describe life at school or college.
Discuss education after 16.
Discuss jobs, career choices and ambitions.
Apply all Foundation grammar plus the Higher Tier additions.
Use the article khana/khani.
Use adjectival postpositions, adjective plus article, and feminine adjective forms.
Use tui, indefinite pronouns, and relative and co-relative pronouns.
Repeat the infinitive for a present participle and use causative verbs.
Combine verbs with dewa, newa, thaka and use the passive with hoa.
Express hypothetical conditions, 'supposed to' and 'while' with verbal nouns and habitual tense.
Use double postpositions.
Use paired conjunctions, if-then conditions, and 'although' clauses.
Use all numbers, ordinals to tenth, minute times and dates.
Recognise spelling variations and most conjuncts at Higher Tier.
Use communication strategies to cope with unknown words.
Ignore words not needed for the main points.
Use layout, pictures and verbal context to infer meaning.
Use grammatical markers and word order to identify word categories.
Use social and cultural context to predict meaning.
Know patterns of word formation: non-finite verb forms, causatives and negative prefixes.
Read and say English loanwords written in Bengali.
Hear aspirated and unaspirated consonant differences and apply understanding strategies in listening.
Use verbal and non-verbal strategies to get meaning across.
Use non-verbal strategies when stuck.
Point and demonstrate with simple phrases.
Use expression and gesture with exclamations.
Use mime, noting its limits in a recorded test.
Use drawing to convey information.
Use verbal strategies when stuck.
Use a word for a similar item.
Describe physical properties of a forgotten item.
Ask for help or translation.
Simplify a form you are unsure of.
Paraphrase to avoid a forgotten word.
Refer to specific features of the item.
Refer to the function of an object.
